Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

result noun and verb

outcome

also outcome, as a result, result in, result from, consequence, implications (likely consequences)

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.42: ēventus est alicujus exitus negōtiī (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 8.29.5: ēventus docuit

ēventus, ēventūs m.

noun, fourth declension

outcome, result

How a thing turns out, well or badly. Latin often says the result with a clause instead: ex quō fit ut, ita fit ut, with the result that; quid ēvēnerit, what came of it.

Other words

  • exitus, exitūs m. — end, outcome

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.22: celerem et facilem exitum habuērunt (Lewis & Short)

  • cōnsequor, cōnsequī, cōnsecūtus sum — follow as a result, result

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.19: ex quō fit ut pudōrem rubor, terrōrem pallor et tremor cōnsequātur (Lewis & Short)

    The result is the subject, the cause the object: blushing “follows” shame.

  • ex quō fit ut — as a result, so that

    phrase: with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 72: ex quō fit, ut animōsior etiam senectūs sit quam adulēscentia; Cic. Off. 1.101: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit

Examples

  • ēventus docuit fortēs fortūnam juvāre

    the result showed that fortune favours the braveLiv. 8.29.5

  • ex quō fit, ut animōsior etiam senectūs sit quam adulēscentia et fortior

    and the result is that old age is bolder and braver even than youthCic. Sen. 72

  • ēventus … stultōrum iste magister est

    the result is the teacher of foolsLiv. 22.39.10

See also effect, cause, happen, actual result, expected result, implication.
